subject: Enablement request: marketplace buying one-pager + common procurement blockers (AWS/GCP)
body:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Enablement request: marketplace buying one-pager + common procurement blockers (AWS/GCP)

Soojin / Markus — we’re getting an uptick in prospects asking to buy via AWS Marketplace (and a smaller but real set via GCP). AEs are struggling to answer procurement questions consistently and we’re losing momentum in late stage.

Can we create a simple “Buying Redwood via Cloud Marketplace” one-pager this week?

What AEs need (minimum):
1) When marketplace is a good fit vs when to push direct contract (esp. discounts / net terms / SLA).
2) What the buyer needs ready (cloud account details, region, who links the org, etc.).
3) SKU selection at a high level (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private + add-ons) with plain English.
4) Common blockers + our recommended responses.
5) Where to send security requests (security packet / SOC2 handling language) and who owns escalation.

Top procurement blockers we’re hearing (examples from HubSpot 41025 + a couple of calls last week):
- “We need an annual commit / spend cap; can we do that via marketplace?”
- “Can you issue a private offer?”
- “What exactly is the invoice line item / product name? Finance needs consistency.”
- “We need proof of SOC 2 / encryption / audit logs before we can buy.”
- “How do upgrades/downgrades work if we start on Hosted via marketplace and later want Dedicated/Private?”

Timing: we have AE enablement next Tue (2/11). If we can get a v0.1 by EOD Thu, I can roll it into that session.

Thanks,
Stephanie

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference



From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Enablement request: marketplace buying one-pager + common procurement blockers (AWS/GCP)

+1. From the SE side, the gaps show up in discovery too.

If we do a one-pager, can we include a “what info to collect” box? AEs keep coming to us after the fact and we end up reworking the purchase/provisioning path.

Proposed “collect upfront” checklist:
- Cloud: AWS vs GCP + buyer account ID / billing account (who will actually click “subscribe”)
- Target Redwood org: do they already have an org? if yes, org slug; if no, who is admin
- Region preference + any residency constraints (US/EU)
- Deployment: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- If Private/VPC: network owner contact + timeline (so we can set expectations)
- Security gating items (NDA required for SOC2 report, pen test letter availability, etc.)

Also: we need crisp language on entitlement activation timing + “what to do if it doesn’t show up.” That’s where we get the angry emails.

Markus

—
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 12:41 PM PT
Subject: Re: Enablement request: marketplace buying one-pager + common procurement blockers (AWS/GCP)

Yes — we can pull this together.

Stephanie: helpful list. Markus: agree on the “collect upfront” box.

Plan:
- I’ll draft the one-pager copy (AWS + GCP) + a short “blockers and answers” appendix for AEs.
- I’ll align the security language with the Marketplace Security FAQ (so we don’t over-claim in the field).

Quick Q before I draft:
1) Do we want the one-pager to cover Private (VPC/on-prem) at a high level, or keep it strictly to Hosted/Dedicated marketplace purchases? (I worry about setting expectations for on-prem via marketplace.)
2) Jordan — can you confirm the current guidance on private offers / discounts via marketplace vs direct?

I’ll share a v0.1 doc tomorrow morning for review.

Soojin

—
Soojin Lee
Product Marketing Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 2:18 PM PT
Subject: Re: Enablement request: marketplace buying one-pager + common procurement blockers (AWS/GCP)

Re: (2) — keep it simple in the one-pager:

- Default path: marketplace for customers that need to apply cloud commit/spend and are okay with published pricing.
- Discounts: we can do private offers in some cases, but don’t promise it. Route to Sales Ops / Finance early.
- If the deal requires non-standard terms (custom SLA, special liability language, big discounting, or complex ramp schedules), we should guide toward direct contract. Marketplace is not the right tool for every enterprise deal.

Also include a line that marketplace purchase doesn’t bypass our security review process for Private/VPC (it’s still a project).

Jordan

—
Jordan Blake
VP, Go-To-Market
Redwood Inference

Co-sign.

One request: make sure this is consistent with the marketplace listing refresh language (no “we are SOC2-certified” type statements; use “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA” etc.). Also avoid anything that reads like a contractual commitment.

If we can land this by Thu, we can include it as part of next week’s internal enablement and then adapt it into a customer-facing FAQ later.

Camila

VP Marketing
Redwood Inference



From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, Feb 5, 2025 at 11:23 AM PT
Subject: Draft: marketplace buying one-pager (v0.3) for AE enablement

Sharing draft for review.

Attachments:
- Redwood_Buying_via_Cloud_Marketplaces_OnePager_v0.3.pdf
- Marketplace_Procurement_Blockers_and_Answers_v0.2.docx

What’s in v0.3:
- “When to use marketplace vs direct” decision box (based on Jordan’s guidance)
- Buyer checklist (cloud acct + Redwood org + region + deployment intent)
- “What to expect after purchase” section (entitlement activation + org linking)
- FAQ: spend caps/commits, private offers (careful language), invoice line item consistency, security packet request flow, upgrades/downgrades

Open items / questions for reviewers:
1) Upgrade/downgrade wording: I wrote this as “contact us; we’ll coordinate the plan transition” to avoid over-committing. Does Sales want something more prescriptive?
2) Invoice description: I used “Redwood Inference — Cloud Marketplace Subscription” as a generic phrase. Finance may have stronger preference.
3) Region/residency: I kept it high-level (“select region during provisioning; availability varies”). Lukas had asked for EU-specific language in other threads — flag if we should add a single EU line.

Stephanie: if you’re good with this, we can use it in the 2/11 enablement as-is and iterate next week.

Soojin

Also, if the one-pager ever gets posted publicly, we should avoid embedding any untagged URLs. I can help with UTMs once we know where it will live.

Ben

- Please add Ben’s tracked contact line.

Otherwise ship it. I’ll present this in the 2/11 enablement and we’ll collect AE feedback.

Thanks everyone.

Stephanie
